steps.content:
August 28th, N.F. 115
West District Second Mine - Field Clinic

A commotion stirs through the work area. A group of young miners is half-carrying, half-dragging a wounded colleague toward the exit. Rumor ripples through the crowd: a rookie, first descent, took a hit of raw contamination to the shoulder. The injured man's face is corpse-pale. Yet, the miners around him look even more terrified.

steps.speaker: Rookie Miner
steps.content: Hey, buddy! You with us? Whoa, easy, easy, the blood's getting everywhere!

steps.speaker: Rookie Miner
steps.content: This is all on me, man. I was yapping away, wasn't paying attention, and now you're hit... I'm so sorry!

steps.speaker: Rookie Miner
steps.content: Just hang tight, okay? I'll grab you something to eat. Specialist's almost here... Lavina!

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Alright, who let their guard down this time?

A red-haired woman strides briskly toward him. Her clothes are plain but neat, and her bright voice carries easily. The lines on her face speak not of weariness, but of a life fully lived, making her warm smile all the more infectious.

Lavina looks even more spirited than he remembers. After the High Tower Black Ring fell, he heard she had left the West District to follow Rustfire and establish contact with the satellite towns. She must have rushed back recently to assist with the post-war reconstruction. Caring for others has always been her calling, after all.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: New around here, aren't you? What's your name? Been at the Drifter Camp before?
No time to invent a name. He gives her his old partner's codename instead. "Thorn's" cover has always been airtight; it won't be compromised.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: "Thorn"? Hmm... don't think I've heard that one. You just started?

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Ah, never mind. Something about how you talk reminds me of my old friends at Rustfire. Must be my imagination.
Of course it does. He spent so long at the Drifter Camp that deliberate effort is required to mask his old habits. He must still be careful not to let her keen intuition pick up on anything.

But this same familiarity also makes it easier to draw out information. Lavina moves through her work while detailing safety protocols, covering procedure after procedure. She chats without a second thought, but he listens with intent, quietly committing every word to memory.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Hm? Asking after Nirvana? Hah, trouble-makers, always will be. Can't drop your guard around them. But it's a sight better than it used to be.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Not all city folk are bad, you know. We've got good friends across the river, too. Even a certain... official, low-profile but quite the big shot, has secured us a lot of resources. Things are smoother now. You just focus on working safe.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Long as you follow the procedure and watch out for each other, you'll be fine.
As she speaks, she ties off the bandage with a practiced knot and pats his shoulder—a gesture both cautionary and encouraging.

The restless pain she once carried has settled into a quiet calm. Time has softened the sorrow from her brow and etched gentle laugh lines at the corners of her eyes... He can't help but feel genuine happiness for her, seeing this change.
Just as the thought settles, someone else lifts the tent flap and steps inside.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Samuel? Weren't you over at Nirvana's sorting things out? What brings you back?

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Matilda's managing it. It's fine. Someone from Decontamination is looking for you. You should go; I'll keep an eye here.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Ugh, they really need to be more careful. I'm on my way.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Oh, and—
She turns back with one last reminder.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Thorn, follow the protocols next time. If I see you in here again, you'll get an earful from me, promise.
The tent flap falls shut. Only Samuel and the "injured worker" remain, and the air grows still.
Samuel looks over. The "newcomer" waits on the cot's edge, wrapped in a coarse cloak, his hair intentionally mussed.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...You make friends quickly.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Comes with being a Syndican.

Rust offers a grin, the kind worn by miners through the dust and ash. The smile doesn't have time to settle before the old man's hand clamps onto his wrist and deftly retrieves a pass concealed beneath the rough fabric.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Syndicans in the mine don't steal. This is Lavina's pass. You lifted it while she was treating you? Quick hands.
Rust stays silent. He's acutely aware of Samuel's weapon, already drawn and leveled at him from beneath the fabric of his cloak.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Word came that someone suspicious had slipped into the shafts, asking questions. That's why I returned early, to meet you. And you even timed it for when I was away. Well-informed. Professional, I take it.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Nirvana's lackey? Or an Outland scout? Who sent you, and what do you want?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Hmm... I'm curious. Who tipped you off?

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: Don't play games. People like you disappear without a trace. Rustfire still has people who can arrange that.

Samuel is the same as ever—sharp and cautious. Crossing paths with him always invites complications. That's precisely why Rust confirmed personnel schedules before he made his move, timing his visit for when Samuel would be away at a meeting. And yet, here they are.
No matter. Adapting is part of the job. The real question is how: concoct another story on the fly, or use the secluded setting to neutralize the problem quietly?
As Rust weighs his options, the light from the entrance flickers. Someone stands at the doorway, holding the tent flap half-open. Before Rust can make out the backlit face, he recognizes the voice.
Sorry, Samuel. He's one of mine.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: ...Chief ${PlayerName}? Then this is...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well, not exactly "one of mine." More like an escapee I couldn't keep tabs on.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Made a bit of a scene saying he was looking for an old friend. Since I care about that friend too, I thought I'd tag along.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A Rustfire intelligence operative—"Rust." Sound familiar, Samuel?
Samuel's hand goes still. Rust catches the brief, distant flicker in his eyes.
It looks, for a moment, like grief.
[Black Screen]

"'Thorn' is Rust's informant and an old friend from the Outlands, also a Sinner."
"He came to DisCity but couldn't locate Rust. He refuses to believe his friend is dead and insists on investigating the truth."
"It's been too long, and information is scarce. If possible, we'd like Rustfire's assistance. This is the only place Rust left any trace."
—Samuel accepts your fabricated story immediately, without a shred of doubt.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: In the autumn of N.F. 113, he supplied us with a great deal of intelligence. Without any single piece of it, we likely couldn't have extracted you from the High Tower Black Ring.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: But I only officially rejoined the organization after the Black Ring fell. Before that, I never had direct contact with him. It wasn't until we compiled the list of the fallen that I even learned his codename.

Though he never met "Rust" in person, Samuel had once compiled a detailed record of every Rustfire member lost in BR-002 over those nine years. Using that, he mapped "Rust's" network—contacts from the Drifter Camp, comrades from Rustfire, scattered Syndicate informants, rival gang affiliates, and more.

The result is a substantial list of leads, which Samuel provides in the hope it will help you learn more about the man you seek.

As you walk the streets of the West District together, your "person of interest" doesn't flee this time. He stays close, cooperating without protest. Perhaps he has finally grasped a few basic truths:

First, if he wants to operate under Rustfire's watch in the West District, working with you is the fastest way. And second—
Just how determined you are to get answers.
[Scene Change] Syndicate Streets

The West District streets, still under reconstruction, thrum with chaotic life. The crowd packs the sidewalks so tightly that the roasted meat bun stalls are doing a roaring trade. Everyone is too busy chasing their next meal to spare a glance at two slightly out-of-place figures seated nearby.
The bun in your hand is delicious, but mixing work with food always dulls the pleasure, especially when the intel you're reviewing only grows more irritating by the minute.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Fake ID, fake ID, fake ID... ALL fake?! Seriously? You spent years here and couldn't make one real friend? Not a single person you could be honest with?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: All those people who still ask about you, who still care... What they're missing is just a character. A performance. Charming lines, rehearsed sincerity... all to play with their feelings. Tch. And these?!!
As you speak, you slide several frayed, handwritten notes from the folder. Each is a personal IOU.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Didn't the 9th Agency approve a budget for you? How do you still owe people money?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: A field agent's budget only covers the basics. I did some research—if you want to build a reliable informant network using money, the real trick is to reverse the dynamic.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You see, people are far more motivated to chase down a debt than to collect a payment. Financial ties, it turns out, bind tighter than sentiment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You sound like someone from Whitestone. Quite the achievement, single-handedly tanking the 9th Agency's reputation.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: That said, I do believe you have a far greater talent for this work than I ever did.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You were the one who spread the word to bring Samuel back, weren't you, Chief? Laid a neat little trap, then swept in just in time to save the day.
A practiced smile rests perfectly on his face.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I'll admit, it was well done. But why go through all the trouble?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You've already put your shackles on me. Could've tracked me and picked me up anytime. I was actually curious why you waited so long to come find me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I just wanted to see what interesting moves you'd make on your own.
You glance at him.

The wound on "Rust's" shoulder clearly isn't from any work accident. Before meeting the workers, he must have already gone down into the mine for his own purposes. Has his objective shifted to BR-002?

But if that were all, he could have simply slipped away afterward. Why go through the trouble of posing as a newcomer and seeking treatment? Gathering intel wouldn't require such theatrics either. Unless...
You'd like to believe he genuinely misses his old friends, but asking directly would never yield an honest answer.

Your terminal vibrates—an update on the joint Black Ring search mission. You skim it. No immediate intervention required. You still have time to humor the stubbornly evasive agent sitting across from you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This place you picked is probably the busiest shop on the street, right? Strong reputation, heavy foot traffic, been here seven years. Prime informant material.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Not on Rustfire's list, so the owner isn't one of theirs. You developed him yourself back when you were with the 9th Agency? He must know more about you than most.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll go have a word with the owner later.
He spreads his hands, offering a gesture that hangs between yielding and daring you to proceed.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Already checked the kitchen. The old owner's gone. All new staff.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: He was in poor health. Whenever we met, I'd bring him the specific medication he needed. Even if his body survived the High Tower Black Ring... he wouldn't have lasted two years without his meds after "Rust" died.
His tone remains as detached as ever, devoid of any sorrow. But his eyes tell a different story: they've softened noticeably.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: He was an interesting man. Bottom-rung Syndican, but proud. If I'd tried to trade medicine for information outright, it would've wounded his pride. He'd have slowly shut me out.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But if I borrowed five hundred from him first, then said "Can't pay you back yet—take this medicine as interest" whenever he came to collect... he'd grumble and curse, but he'd take it. Even slipped me extra food now and then, treating me like the broke fool I was pretending to be.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: And while we were chatting about this and that... I'd coax out quite a bit of intelligence.

His gaze settles on the roasted meat buns on the table, freshly made, generously stuffed and fragrant. The agent has ordered a dipping sauce with an unusual mix of ingredients to go with them. The flavor is quite good, actually. You've eaten them all.
Food steeped in memory has a way of softening hearts. The pointed exchanges from moments ago no longer seem to matter.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you cooperate when we go back to the Bureau, I might even keep ordering takeout for you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Please, spare me. I've told you everything I can. The rest... let's call it privacy, shall we?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I've nothing against you personally, Chief. But given how much EDGE values you, who knows what they've put in you? I'd rather not have an audience listening in.
As his smile fades, so does the nostalgia in his eyes. He pushes the buns back toward you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: The one who loved these was "Rust" of the 9th Agency. That body is gone. This is a new vessel, so time to develop new tastes.
You're still searching for the right words when your terminal buzzes. A message from the 9th Agency cuts through the silence:

New lead, and a major breakthrough!

We've tracked Underground movements. They haven't pinpointed BR-003, but are actively investigating the other Black Rings. Interception team preparing to deploy. Exact coordinates...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: See? Duty calls. An urgent dispatch from the 9th Agency, I presume.
It clicks immediately. The breakthrough is his design. This is a game, and like you did with Samuel, Rust is now moving you across the board.
Dragging him to MBCC is an option, but too blunt. Without understanding his driver, he'd escape again.
Letting him go to trace the shackles later feels like falling into a prepared script. He's likely arranged for that, too.
...Confrontation, then? Right here, with all cards on the table?
He reads your hesitation, your silent debate. A soft chuckle escapes him before he voices a proposal that changes the entire equation.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: There's still time. Why not take a walk with me, Chief?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: These streets are where "Rust" once lived. If you want to find out the man he was... this is the place to do it.
You have the time, and so you see no reason to refuse.
[Scene Change]

The two of you walk through the dusk-lit streets, the afterglow deepening around you. No matter how much the West District has changed, for all these years the sunset has painted these streets in the same crimson hues.
It also lends a flush of warmth to his pale face, making him look, for a moment, a little less different from those around him.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: This place has changed so much. For the better, too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The Ash Campaign destroyed many parts of the city. Otherwise, you'd be seeing something even more impressive.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: The tensions with Nirvana and Eastside... they're still there, aren't they? Have you been mediating this whole time?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I can't take that much credit. It's mostly Matilda and the rest of the Executive Committee doing the heavy lifting.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Miss Cavendish is quite reliable, yes. But without the Bureau's "back channels," I doubt so many of those "Rustfire rioters" would have avoided prosecution and regained their freedom.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I heard Mr. Donald moved to a satellite town? Do the two of you still keep in touch?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We do, just not as often. Everyone's busy.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But you could visit them. Don would be happy to see you. Samuel mentioned you two crossed paths back in N.F. 113.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Heh, that was the old "Rust." I'm not that free. Making it to the West District is already pushing my limits. I'll just have to pick up news about them while I'm here.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Lavina and Samuel are doing quite well, it seems. Just now, "Mama Lavina" mentioned she had a video call last week with a kid who just returned to the Bureau.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hah, it must be her. She's been studying, but after running around outside for a bit, she came back having forgotten how to write half her characters. Then she just went on and on about needing to call Lavina and catch up with her.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But her health isn't great. Ever since she came out of the Black Ring, she's needed constant rest. She sleeps for long stretches, and no one can figure out why.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Once your consciousness has merged with a Black Ring, breaking free is no simple task. It takes everything you have.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But she made it back. That's what matters. My guess is she sleeps so long because she's trying to find someone in her dreams, to go back for them. Once she finds who she's looking for, she won't need to keep at it. She'll perk right up.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Or perhaps... there's a simpler explanation. You've assigned her such a heavy course load that little Hella has no choice but to fake an illness to escape her studies?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hiding from Raven? She's running a proper Syndicate Academy now, and enrollment is booming. It's been two years already. Time changes a lot of things.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Is that so?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I guess it really does.

He smiles, but his pace gradually slows until he stops in the middle of the street. The sunset bathes him in gold as the crowd flows past, their faces bright with genuine laughter, a stark contrast to his own stillness. He simply stands there, watching.
You stop as well and turn to face him. Just as you're about to speak, your terminal buzzes again. You let out a quiet sigh.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I know you're the one who fed them that intel. Send me on a wild goose chase so you could slip away, right? Thanks for the assist—still frustrating as hell, though.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Being honest wouldn't kill you. You obviously came back because you missed them. I really don't get what you're so set on hiding.
He holds vital intel. You carry a heavy debt to him. After all this time, you've finally found him. The questions are pressing, yet...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Forget it. Even if you don't say anything, I'll find out what I need on my own. But don't think you can run. Once I'm done here, I will find you. Doesn't matter how many times you die, how many shells you swap, what mission you take next.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This isn't about work. Or any official interrogation. It's about you—
You don't get to finish. A sharp shout from behind cuts through the conversation.

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: Hey—!! Was that—was that your order just now?

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: This sauce... this sauce... is it yours?!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Uh... It's a friend of mine...

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: I knew it! It's "Rust," isn't it! That old-school ratio—I'd know it anywhere! Two years, not a word, and my old boss griped about the money he owed right up 'til the end! Is he ever gonna pay up or what?!

This sparks a fierce tirade from the shop owner—phrases and grievances that must have been passed down from his late boss. You add a few corroborating comments to keep the rhythm going, then smoothly slide him some new details: Rust went to a satellite town, looking for work to earn some money.

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: ...Honestly, just knowing he's alright is enough. He was a regular, you know? My old boss thought about him for two whole years, came up with new dishes he never got to try. If you see him... tell him to visit. I can at least try to cook a few of the old ones.

steps.speaker: Shop Owner
steps.content: But most importantly, he still owes us! Fifty DisCoins!
With a light laugh, you send the shop owner off, then glance toward Rust.
An agent with his people skills should know how to read a room. And if he somehow misses it, Samuel already spelled things out plainly enough.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: If you hear anything about him, good or bad, let us know.

steps.speaker: Samuel
steps.content: He'll always be a friend of Rustfire.
He absorbs your words in utter silence, waiting for you to finish before he finally offers a reply.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...You certainly have a way with words. Whether it's winning people over or pulling intel out of them. A real professional.
Bzzz— Your terminal vibrates again.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Go ahead and take the mission, Chief. I've held you up long enough. What I have left to say... it's honest. And it won't take long.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I may carry traces of the Underground, but I'm not your enemy. Everything I do is to repel the Black Rings, to stop the fanatics spreading them. If our goals align, I'm willing to lend a hand when I can.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Tell EDGE to be careful. You've successfully recovered BR-002 and BR-005, but BR-003's existence is exposed. The enemy will move soon.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: What they're after is BR-003's true core: that inheritance fragment that has successfully merged with the Corpus... So don't get attached to whatever benefits the Black Ring offers. Deal with it quickly, while EDGE still has a weapon like you on the field.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But when you're out there... remember: at the final moment, don't use your shackles to make contact like before. Don't let "instinct" tempt you into accepting it. That... wouldn't end well. You're strong enough as it is. Any further, and you'll be stepping into dangerous territory.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Leave it to EDGE. Just like with BR-002 and BR-005, destroy the Black Ring, recover the "fragment," purify it, and seal it away. Guard it well. As long as it's not taken, there won't be a problem.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You could've told me all this sooner, you know.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: An agent doesn't hand over information freely. Intel is worth more than one's life. I had to build trust carefully—with you, and with every organization behind you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So you're saying you didn't trust me before? Or are you telling me you suddenly trust everyone behind me now?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I've always trusted you... and I will never trust <color=#fb9259>them</color>. But now, I believe it doesn't matter who stands behind you. It won't be a problem.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...That's a lot to take in. I need some time to process this.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: That's fine. If it's hard to trust me, just pass the message along.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Tell my former supervisor at the 9th Agency, or... let the EDGE technology buried inside you hear it clearly. They'll make the call.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Also, there's something I'd like to ask of you. Consider it... an exchange of favors.
He pauses for a long moment, as though gathering his thoughts with exacting care. Then, slowly, he begins—one request at a time.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: First, for Samuel: at 85 East Street in the Drifter Camp, second floor, third compartment. Under the third floorboard on the upper left, he'll find some detection manuals. Have him use them at the mine. If anything unusual comes up, run a patrol sweep immediately. That's the only way to root out the truly dangerous ones in time.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: With it, there's also a sealed letter. It's a will that "Rust" wrote to "Thorn" ahead of time. But the death came too suddenly... I never had the chance to deliver it. I'll have to ask you to do it for me.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Tell Thorn not to blame himself so much. "Rust" fell fighting the Underground. He never had any regrets, and for his partner, he had nothing but gratitude.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Rather than revenge, "Rust" would prefer Thorn to visit the cemetery when there's time. Bring a few bottles of good wine, and some roasted meat buns from the old shop.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Also... everything you noted he owed during your visit earlier, please help settle it all.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: My apologies for the cost. Rust's survivor benefits should still be valid. See if you can claim them to cover the debts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Why are you asking me to do all this?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Why... I suppose even I didn't expect that "Rust," two years gone, would be lucky enough to make such a stubborn friend.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: It's your fault, you know. For being so stubborn. For insisting on pulling him back here, making him revisit every regret, live through such a happy day... only to face another painful goodbye.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: It's too much for him to carry. So please, take responsibility and see it through for him. He would be truly grateful.
That wasn't your question. Yet his answer is so disarmingly sincere that it catches you off guard, and you let him continue without interruption.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Thank you. The Black Rings are a terminal illness of our time, but you've shown me that a cure might be possible.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Thank you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Keep this in mind: no matter where you go, how many times you die, what body you use, or what your mission is... you are my friend.
He listens with genuine attention, his expression softening into a smile meant just for you.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Then... let's save the rest for next time. Don't worry; with the shackles, you can always find me.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I wish you all the best, Chief ${PlayerName}.

In the following days, you successfully root out several Underground scouts lurking in the BR-005 ruins. Other operatives closing in on the archives to steal BR-003 intelligence are neutralized as well. Bolstered by timely intel from an anonymous source, every operation proceeds smoothly.

Back at the Bureau, as you're weighing your next move regarding the "interrogation," you receive an unexpected update: an intelligence access request filed a few days ago has been approved. The file from the 9th Agency, marked top-secret, arrives.

[9th Agency Top-Secret Archive Excerpt-0]

No Security Classification  Not for Public Disclosure
—Experiment and Surveillance Records of Underground Fugitive S-247.
He bids farewell to the warm sun, the bustling streets, to those who pursued him and those who showed him kindness—returning, at last, to a place even more familiar.

steps.speaker: Undergrounder C
steps.content: To sabotage our plans with such precision... I knew it had to be you.

steps.speaker: Undergrounder C
steps.content: You returned unusually fast this time. Was it the Fifth Black Ring that reshaped you?

steps.speaker: Undergrounder C
steps.content: ...And arrogant as ever. You still dare to come here—and alone, no less.
He opens his eyes, and is greeted once more by the people he knows all too well.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But of course. You are the very reason I cling to this wretched existence.
